_doc: Peru, written by hand for the plans hour by hour (Manu, 2026-11-12). Same format as todo.json; steps = the day hour by hour, extras = what the tour programmes leave out, sights = places of the globe each thing covers.

areas.season: It almost never rains. June to October is grey and cool under the garúa mist (15–19 °C); December to March is sunny and warm (25–29 °C).
areas.sleep: Miraflores or Barranco: by the sea, safe to walk, near the restaurants. See the historic centre by day.

items.name: Miraflores clifftops and Barranco at sunset
items.why: The Pacific from the cliffs, then the old bohemian quarter, its bridge and its bars. The easiest first evening in Peru.

steps.what: Walk the Malecón from Parque Kennedy to Parque del Amor
Sunset over the Pacific from the clifftop or Larcomar

steps.note: Puente de los Suspiros and the steps down to the sea
Peruvians dine late; book the popular places

items.name: Historic centre: Plaza Mayor, the Cathedral and San Francisco's catacombs
items.best: Morning; the guard changes at the Government Palace around noon
items.why: The colonial heart of the viceroyalty: balconies, the Cathedral with Pizarro's tomb, and the bone-lined crypts under San Francisco.

steps.what: Taxi from Miraflores to Plaza Mayor
San Francisco monastery and its catacombs
steps.note: guided visits in English and Spanish, about 45 min

steps.what: Changing of the guard at the Government Palace, Plaza Mayor
Lunch: ceviche back in Miraflores or near the centre

extras: Walk down Jirón de la Unión to Plaza San Martín: the art deco square few tours bother with.
Keep the phone in the pocket around the centre's busy streets.

items.name: Larco Museum
items.best: Late afternoon; it stays open into the evening
items.why: Pre-Columbian Peru in one house: gold, textiles and thousands of Moche pots. The best start before Cusco.
extras: The garden café is one of the city's nicest lunches.

items.name: Huaca Pucllana, an adobe pyramid in Miraflores
items.why: A 1,500-year-old pyramid of mud bricks in the middle of the city's smartest district.

items.name: Pachacamac
items.best: Morning, before the sun is high
items.why: A huge sanctuary of temples and pyramids used for a thousand years before the Incas, at the edge of the desert.

items.name: The Magic Water Circuit
items.why: Lit fountains and a water show in the Parque de la Reserva. Locals love it.

extras: Ceviche is lunch in Lima: the classic cevicherías close in the late afternoon.
From the airport to Miraflores takes 45 min to 1 h 30. Before a domestic flight at rush hour, leave 3 h ahead.
Surquillo market, next to Miraflores, is where cooks shop: fruit you have never seen, cheap lunch counters.

areas.season: Desert: sunny almost all year, hazier and cooler from June to September. A strong wind (the paraca) often rises in the afternoon.
areas.sleep: In Paracas by the bay for the morning boat, or at the Huacachina oasis for the dunes. Ica, 5 km from Huacachina, has more choice.

items.name: Ballestas Islands by boat
items.best: First boat around 08:00: the sea is calm in the morning
items.book: Book the day before; boats leave from El Chaco pier
items.why: Sea lions, Humboldt penguins and boobies by the thousand on bare rock islands, and the giant Candelabra drawn on the hill on the way.

steps.note: pay the small port fee and the island fee in cash

steps.what: Boat out; stop at the Candelabra geoglyph
Around the islands: sea lions, penguins, boobies
Back on the pier; breakfast by the bay

extras: Wear a hat: thousands of birds fly over the boat.
A windproof layer: the boat is fast and the morning is cool.

items.name: Paracas National Reserve: red beach and cliffs
items.best: Late morning, after the boat; the wind rises in the afternoon
items.why: Pink and ochre desert falling into the ocean, the red beach and fishing villages where you eat what came in that morning.

steps.what: Drive into the reserve; visitor centre

steps.note: its arch fell in the 2007 earthquake

items.name: Huacachina: dune buggy and sandboarding
items.best: Late afternoon, for the sunset from the dunes
items.book: Any agency at the oasis; choose one with seat belts
items.why: A lagoon in a ring of giant dunes. The buggy is a roller coaster; the boards go down on your belly.

steps.what: Buggy into the dunes; sandboarding on 3–4 slopes
Sunset from the top of the dunes
Dinner by the lagoon or in Ica

extras: Ica is pisco country: a bodega tasting on the way costs little and few tours stop.
Sand gets into everything: a cheap bag for the phone.
Many tours do Ballestas, the reserve and Huacachina in one day from Lima: it works, but it is 12 hours on the move.
Bring cash in soles: the pier, the reserve and the oasis rarely take cards.

areas.season: Hot and dry all year. Flights are best in the morning, before the wind and the heat haze.
areas.sleep: One night in town is enough. Many take the lines in the morning and leave for Arequipa by night bus.

items.name: Nazca Lines from the air
items.hours: 35 min flight · 2–3 h with the waiting
items.book: Book with an operator with a good safety record; bring the passport
items.why: The hummingbird, the monkey, the spider: figures hundreds of metres long, only readable from the sky.

steps.what: At María Reiche airfield: passport and weighing

steps.note: flights go by weight and wind
the plane banks left and right so both sides see

extras: A light breakfast only: the small plane turns hard.
Not flying? The roadside tower on the Panamericana shows the Hands and the Tree from the ground for a few soles.

items.name: Chauchilla Cemetery
items.why: Mummies still sitting in their open tombs in the desert, with hair and cloth after a thousand years.

items.name: Cantalloc aqueducts
items.why: Spiral stone wells the Nazca people built to reach water underground. Some still run.

extras: The night bus to Arequipa takes about 9–10 hours: book a semi-cama or cama seat.

areas.season: Sunny almost every day; cool nights. A little rain from January to March. The city is at 2,335 m.
areas.sleep: In the historic centre, within walking distance of the Plaza de Armas.

items.name: Yanahuara viewpoint and El Misti at sunset
items.why: White stone arches framing the perfect cone of El Misti. The classic Arequipa view.

items.name: Santa Catalina Monastery, the Plaza de Armas and Juanita
items.hours: A whole day, at an easy pace
items.best: Start at Santa Catalina in the morning
items.why: A walled city of nuns in red and blue streets, the white-stone square, and Juanita, the Inca girl found frozen on Ampato.

steps.note: 2 h; take a guide at the door (paid on top)

steps.what: Plaza de Armas and the Cathedral

steps.note: rocoto relleno, chupe de camarones; they serve lunch only

steps.what: Museo Santuarios Andinos: Juanita, the ice maiden
Sunset from Yanahuara if not done yet

items.name: Colca Canyon in a day
items.best: Only if you can't sleep in Chivay; two days is much better
items.why: The condors at Cruz del Cóndor without sleeping in the canyon. A very long day, over a 4,900 m pass.

extras: Arequipa (2,335 m) is a good step up before Colca (3,600 m and a 4,900 m pass) and Puno (3,830 m).
Queso helado, a cinnamon ice cream sold by the Santa Catalina wall, is the local snack.

areas.season: Dry and sunny from April to November, freezing nights. Rain from December to March. Chivay is at 3,630 m.
areas.sleep: In Chivay or Yanque: a lodge with hot springs makes the cold night easy.

items.name: Cruz del Cóndor at dawn, the terraced valley on the way back
items.best: 08:00–10:00, when the condors rise on the warm air
items.why: Andean condors riding the morning air out of one of the deepest canyons on Earth, a few metres over your head.

steps.what: Yanque square: morning dances, then Maca's church

steps.note: stay at least an hour; walk the rim path away from the crowd

steps.what: Back along the canyon; terraces viewpoints at Pinchollo and Antahuilque

extras: Fewer condors in the rainy months (December to March).
The tourist ticket (boleto) for the canyon is checked on the road: carry cash soles.

items.name: La Calera hot springs
items.best: Evening of the day you arrive
items.why: Hot pools by the river after the long drive from Arequipa.
extras: The road from Arequipa crosses Patapampa at about 4,900 m: coca tea, little food, no alcohol that day.

items.name: Uyo Uyo ruins and a walk in Yanque
items.why: Stone houses of the Collagua people and terraces still farmed, ten minutes from Chivay.

extras: Fit and with time: the two-day trek down to the Sangalle oasis from Cabanaconde, 1,000 m down and up again at dawn.
From Chivay to Puno is about 6 hours over the altiplano, with flamingos at Lagunillas.

areas.season: At 3,830 m: sunny days and freezing nights all year. Rain in the afternoon from December to March.
areas.sleep: In Puno near the Plaza de Armas, or a lodge on the lake. One night with a family on Amantaní is the real thing.

items.name: Sillustani burial towers at sunset
items.why: Stone towers of the Colla lords on a peninsula over Lake Umayo. The late light makes them glow.

items.name: Uros and Taquile by boat
items.why: Islands made of reeds, then Taquile, where the men knit and the textiles are on UNESCO's list.

steps.note: about 1 h; they show how the islands are built

steps.what: Lunch with a family: lake trout
Down the long stone stairway to the other port

extras: The sun on the lake is strong: hat and sun cream even when it feels cold.
Bring small coins for the islands' boat rides and crafts.

items.name: A night with a family on Amantaní
items.book: Through a Puno agency or a community tour
items.why: Sleep in a farmhouse, eat what the family eats, sunset from the Pachatata temple. Taquile on the way back.

extras: Puno is at 3,830 m: the first evening, rest, coca tea, light dinner.
Candelaria, one of South America's biggest festivals, fills Puno with dancers in the first half of February.
The tourist bus to Cusco (about 10 h) stops at Pukará, La Raya pass (4,335 m), Raqchi and Andahuaylillas: a sightseeing day, not just a transfer.

areas.season: Dry and sunny from May to September, below 0 °C at night. Rain most afternoons from December to March. The city is at 3,400 m.
areas.sleep: San Blas or near the Plaza de Armas, on foot to everything. San Blas is steep: think of it with luggage.

items.name: A slow first afternoon in San Blas
items.why: The altitude needs a gentle first day: craft workshops, the twelve-angled stone and the view over the roofs.

steps.what: Coca tea, then walk down Hatun Rumiyoc to the twelve-angled stone
San Blas square and its workshops
steps.note: the church pulpit is carved from one cedar

steps.what: Sunset from the San Blas viewpoint
Light dinner, no alcohol the first night

items.name: Cusco on foot: market, Qorikancha, the Cathedral
items.best: Start at the market, before the crowds
items.why: The Inca capital under the Spanish one: walls of the Sun temple inside a convent, and a cathedral full of Andean paintings.

steps.note: fruit juice at the counters, the stalls of herbs and bread

steps.what: Plaza de Armas and the Cathedral
steps.note: about 1 h 30; look for the guinea pig on the Last Supper

steps.what: Lunch: a set menu of the day in a local place
Pre-Columbian Art Museum or the Inka Museum
Evening walk in the lit square; pisco on a balcony

extras: Qorikancha and the Cathedral are not on the tourist ticket: pay at the door.
Many churches let you in free for the morning mass: quiet, no ticket, no photos.

items.name: Sacsayhuamán and the ruins above town, walking down
items.best: Afternoon; take a taxi up and walk down
items.why: The giant zigzag walls of Sacsayhuamán and three smaller Inca sites, done downhill as the locals do.

steps.what: Taxi to Tambomachay, the highest of the four
Tambomachay's water channels, Puka Pukara across the road
Walk down to Qenqo, a carved rock shrine

steps.note: walls of stones over 100 tonnes; 1 h 30

steps.what: Down the old stone path into San Blas at sunset

extras: Above Sacsayhuamán, the White Christ (Cristo Blanco) has the best free view over the city.

items.name: Sacred Valley by road: Pisac, Moray, Maras, Chinchero
items.book: Tourist ticket for Pisac, Moray and Chinchero; Maras salt pans paid at the gate
items.why: Terraces on a mountain, the circular Inca terraces of Moray and 3,000 salt pools on a hillside.

steps.note: enter from the top car park and walk down

extras: Sunday is the big market day in Pisac.
Better still: sleep a night in the valley and go on to Machu Picchu from Ollantaytambo.

items.name: Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca)
items.best: After 2–3 days in Cusco, not before
items.book: A day or two ahead; cash for the community fee
items.why: Striped red, yellow and green slopes at about 5,000 m. Unforgettable when clear, hard on the lungs.

steps.note: horses can take you most of the way up, paid in cash

extras: Palccoyo, another rainbow mountain, is about 1 h of easy walking with far fewer people.
The Red Valley next to Vinicunca is worth the extra 30 minutes if your legs hold.

items.name: Humantay Lake
items.why: A turquoise lake under the Salkantay glacier, after a steep 1 h 30 climb to 4,200 m.

extras: The tourist ticket (boleto turístico) costs S/130 and covers 16 sites for 10 days, not Machu Picchu, Qorikancha, the Cathedral or Maras.
Machu Picchu tickets are sold by the hour (06:00 to 15:00) and by circuit at tuboleto.cultura.pe: in high season buy weeks ahead.
The Inca Trail needs a permit bought through an agency, months ahead; the trail closes every February.
Inti Raymi, the Inca sun festival, fills Sacsayhuamán on 24 June: book everything early that week.

areas.season: Lower and warmer than Cusco (2,800–2,900 m). Dry from May to September; rain in the afternoon from December to March.
areas.sleep: Ollantaytambo for the trains to Machu Picchu and the Inca streets; Urubamba for lodges with gardens.

items.name: Ollantaytambo fortress at opening time, then the Inca town
items.best: 07:00, before the tour buses arrive mid-morning
items.why: Terraces and the unfinished Sun temple over a town whose Inca canals still run down the streets.

steps.what: Up the terraces to the Sun temple
Across town, up to the Pinkuylluna storehouses
The Inca blocks of the old town

items.name: Moray and the Maras salt pans, walking down to the river
items.best: Afternoon light on the salt pans
items.book: Moray on the tourist ticket; Maras paid at the gate
items.why: Circular Inca terraces, then thousands of salt pools on a hillside, still worked by local families.

steps.what: Walk down from the salt pans to the Urubamba river
steps.note: about 1 h; a taxi waits at the bridge

extras: The walk down from the salt pans is not in most tours: the best view of the pools.

items.name: Pisac ruins from the top, walking down to the market
items.best: Morning; Sunday is the big market
items.why: Some of the finest Inca terraces anywhere, then the market. Done top-down, it's all downhill.

steps.what: Taxi to the upper car park
Walk the ridge: Intihuatana, the terraces
Down the stairs to the village

items.name: Chinchero: weavers and the Sunday market
items.why: A colonial church on Inca walls and women who dye wool with plants in front of you.

extras: Trains to Machu Picchu leave from Ollantaytambo (PeruRail, Inca Rail), about 1 h 30 to Aguas Calientes.
On the train only a small bag (about 5 kg): leave the big one at the hotel in Ollantaytambo or Cusco.
Fit and keen: the one-day Inca Trail from km 104 reaches Machu Picchu through the Sun Gate; it needs a permit too.

areas.season: Cloud forest at 2,000–2,400 m: humid, warm by day. Rain most afternoons from November to March; early clouds often lift by 9–10.
areas.sleep: One night in Aguas Calientes lets you take an early bus up and miss the day trippers.

items.name: Aguas Calientes hot springs
items.why: Simple hot pools at the end of the town's main street, after the train.

items.name: Machu Picchu on the first buses
items.best: An early slot, or a 9–10 slot when the morning is cloudy
items.book: Ticket with time slot and circuit, bus ticket, passport
items.why: The Inca city on its ridge, mist rising off the peaks. Circuits are one-way: you walk the route on your ticket once.

steps.note: the first leaves at 05:30; 25 min up

steps.what: Through the gate with your guide
The postcard view from the upper terraces
Temple of the Sun, the royal quarter, the Intihuatana (depending on circuit)
Bus down; breakfast in Aguas Calientes

extras: Toilets are only outside the gate: go before you enter.
Big backpacks stay in the lockers at the entrance.
Insect repellent: tiny biting flies by the ruins.
Some circuits include the walk to the Sun Gate (Intipunku), where the Inca Trail arrives: about 2 h return, worth it if yours does.

items.name: Huayna Picchu or Machu Picchu Mountain
items.best: Its own time slot on the ticket
items.book: Buy with the Machu Picchu ticket: few places a day
items.why: The peak in the photos, climbed on Inca stairs, looking down on the whole city. Huayna is steep and exposed.

items.name: Mandor gardens and waterfall
items.why: Flat walk along the railway into a private garden with orchids, birds and a waterfall.

extras: Entry is with a licensed guide; guides wait at the bridge and the gate.
Buses down run all day; walking down the steps takes about 1 h 30.

areas.season: Rainforest: 25–33 °C and humid. Wettest from December to March, when trails are mud; drier May to October.
areas.sleep: In a lodge up the Tambopata or Madre de Dios river. Lodges run the days: boats, guides and meals included.

items.name: Night walk in the forest
items.why: Tarantulas, frogs and stick insects by torchlight, a few minutes from the lodge.

items.name: Lake Sandoval by canoe
items.why: An oxbow lake with giant river otters, caimans, hoatzins and macaws flying over.

steps.what: Paddle the lake: otters fish early

items.name: Macaws at the clay lick
items.why: Hundreds of red and green macaws and parrots landing on a river cliff to eat clay. Dry mornings only.

steps.what: Parrots, then the macaws on the clay

items.name: Canopy tower at sunrise or sunset
items.why: Above the trees, toucans and monkeys at eye level.

extras: Long sleeves and long trousers in light colours, against the mosquitoes. Lodges lend rubber boots.
Yellow fever vaccination is recommended for this region: check with a travel clinic weeks ahead.
Flights from Cusco take under an hour: an easy add-on to Machu Picchu.

areas.season: Dry and sunny from May to September, the trekking season. Rain from December to March. Huaraz is at 3,050 m.
areas.sleep: In Huaraz town; agencies pick up from hotels for all day trips.

items.name: Laguna Churup, the acclimatisation hike
items.why: A green lake under a peak at 4,450 m: the classic test before Laguna 69.

items.name: Laguna 69
items.why: A turquoise lake under the glaciers of Chacraraju, past the Llanganuco lakes. One of Peru's great day hikes.
extras: The last hour is steep and the air is thin: start at the front of the group.

items.name: Pastoruri glacier and the Puya raimondii
items.why: A retreating glacier at 5,000 m and giant puya plants that flower once in a century.

items.name: Chavín de Huántar
items.why: Tunnels and carved stone heads of a culture 3,000 years old, across the Cordillera.

extras: Huaraz is at 3,050 m and Laguna 69 at 4,600 m: two easy days first is not optional.
